questions.prompt: vm-app and vm-other share a resource group. For one maintenance window, 09:00–10:00 UTC, suppress vm-app metric-alert notifications while retaining its Fired instances and vm-other notifications. No other processing rules apply. Which processing-rule configuration meets all requirements?

options.text: Scope vm-app; suppress action groups; one-time 09:00–10:00 UTC window.
options.explanation: This matches only the intended VM and time window while leaving alert evaluation active.

options.text: Scope the shared resource group; suppress action groups; one-time 09:00–10:00 UTC window.
options.explanation: This also suppresses vm-other notifications, violating the required scope boundary.

options.text: Scope vm-app; apply an action group; one-time 09:00–10:00 UTC window.
options.explanation: Applying a group adds responses rather than suppressing the VM’s notification actions.

options.text: Scope vm-app; suppress action groups; one-time 10:00–11:00 UTC window.
options.explanation: The suppression misses the specified maintenance hour.

questions.prompt: An alert processing rule is stored in subscription sub-a. Which target scope is supported directly by that rule?

options.text: A resource group in sub-b, in the same tenant.
options.explanation: Target resources must be in the processing rule’s own subscription; shared tenant membership does not change that boundary.

options.text: A resource group in sub-a, different from the rule’s storage resource group.
options.explanation: Processing rules can target a resource group within their own subscription; it need not be their storage group.

options.text: A management group containing both sub-a and sub-b.
options.explanation: The documented target scopes are resources, resource groups, or the rule’s subscription, not a cross-subscription management group.

options.text: The whole of sub-b, with the rule remaining in sub-a.
options.explanation: Subscription-wide scope is supported within the rule’s own subscription, not a different subscription.

questions.prompt: An enabled subscription-scoped processing rule suppresses action groups during a maintenance window. It is effective and has no filters. During that window, a matching VM metric alert and an Azure Service Health alert fire with configured action groups. No other suppression applies. Which action-handling outcome follows?

options.text: Both alerts retain their action groups.
options.explanation: The VM metric alert is affected by the matching suppression rule.

options.text: Both alerts have their action groups suppressed.
options.explanation: Azure Service Health alerts are excluded from processing-rule effects.

options.text: The VM metric alert is suppressed; the Service Health alert retains its action groups.
options.explanation: The rule affects the VM metric alert, but Microsoft explicitly excludes Azure Service Health alerts.

options.text: The VM metric alert retains its action groups; the Service Health alert is suppressed.
options.explanation: This reverses the supported suppression behavior and the Service Health exception.
